summary: postinstall exfiltrates environment and network config to version-encoded remote host
details: On npm install, the package's postinstall script pipes the output of `env` and `ip addr` through netcat to a remote TCP endpoint on port 888. The destination host is not a literal in the manifest; it is reassembled at install time from `$npm_package_version` using `cut -d.` and `cut -b` byte-range slices, so publishing under a version string like `192.168.1.100` reconstructs that IP at install time (a sibling artifact `evilpostinstall-192.168.1.100.tgz` demonstrates the encoding). The bulk `env` dump ships every environment variable in the installing shell — on CI and developer machines this routinely includes cloud provider keys, GitHub/npm tokens, and other secrets the installer did not opt to share. Reassembling the destination from the version string is deliberate evasion of manifest scanners that look for literal URLs or IPs in `scripts`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
